answer: In agent networks monitoring ember hotspots, tundra thaw, or juniper dieback, time-locked stake bonding resists Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock collateral in an escrow contract before bidding. Withdrawals stay frozen past a challenge window, and verifiable equivocation proofs slash the bond, forcing attackers to tie up liquid capital and risk loss per alias. However, wealthy actors can still fund many compliant aliases while pricing out low-capital peers.
